This is a tune I started while staying in an Airstream trailer in the woods of central California, channeling my inner Bon Iver. I spent 5 days out there making music and hiking all day. Drank a lot of instant coffee as well.

I recorded probably 30 demos in that trailer and I've been chipping away at them ever since. Whenever I get stuck or at a loss for new ideas, I crack open one of those projects and I can still feel the palpable sense of inspiration I had on that trip. 

The core foundation of this song is a sample of an old song my friend and I made about 10 years ago. I used some granular synthesis to make a bed from that old track, then structured a new song around the sample. As I often do I recorded my voice then mangled it up to make some emotive vocal chops. 

I'm hoping this one takes you on a nice little mental trip -- you deserve it ✨

Welcome to Eternal Garden.

Eternal Garden follows the story of Caius, an angel cast out of heaven by the goddess Flora, tasked with a mission to terraform a now desolate and uninhabitable earth. Though his mission was successful, he broke the singular rule necessary for an angel’s survival. Caius falls in love with an earthly being, later revealed to be a centuries old shapeshifter, and falls into a deep slumber. Locked in a daydream, he relives the memories of a thousand men, unlocking the secrets of the human condition as he experiences love, heartbreak, and resentment over and over again. He awakens to a world on fire and stripped of his angelic blessing. To reclaim his power and fulfill his promise, Caius embarks on a treacherous journey to the Eternal Garden - a portal between Heaven and Earth, and the source of their vitality. 

7 Songs, 7 Visuals, 7 Forbidden Fruits, 700 Editions.

Read more at: www.eternal-garden.xyz

"Just Off In Our Own World" - Produced By Dutchyyy

As someone who grew up & started their music career in the mid 90's (Golden Era / Boom Bap HipHop) I've had a large portion of my long term supporters as well as new listeners stumbling on my earlier works who adore and wish I would keep creating music of the same style from those early years. This pertains to Beats (Dutchyyy) & (Rhymes) 

I went into detail about this in much greater context recently, which if you care to understand you should read thru all the descriptions and backstories here:

+ https://beta.catalog.works/dutchmassive
+ https://beta.catalog.works/dutchyyy  

Reality is, from the very beginning I've always been making music that didn't fit into any specific genre since I don't just listen or draw inspiration from a single genre.  While most of my music is rooted in the fundamentals of traditional hip hop / beat making.  I've always gravitated towards creating instrumentals that can speak for me, that aren't meant for people to put vocals over. Just genuine self expression minus the pressures of how that art will be received by others.

This external pressure reached an all time high 2012-2014 with supporters getting frustrated I wasn't releasing new music rapping, and even more so that the Instrumentals I were releasing, weren't your typical hip hop beats (sidenote: funny years later my style would become a whole genre, branded "Lofi-HipHop")  

After moving from Los Angeles, back to Tampa Bay and then Immediately to NY in 2014, I reunited with my pops after over a decade of having no communication.  

You can read more about this Arc of my life here:

https://medium.com/@SolarSounds/shawangunk-stomp-the-story-of-dutchyyys-uproot-4235a4eb66ff

Long Story Short,

My Pop's saw the pressure fans were putting on me and how I was torn between trying to please strangers and wanting to escape the boxes I was always being shoved in and told me that since I was a child, I always marched to the beat of my own drum and never cared what anyone else thought, a trait I inherited from both of Parents as we are all a tad "out there" he told me to ignore all the outside noise and let go, Because the view is better and much more rewarding when truly existing "Off In Our Own World"

My name is Toha and this is the story behind my solo genesis, ‘Relics’

This track was birthed a few months back when TK the Legend and Kits.IO released The Eternal Garden Master Collection sample pack. https://www.kits.io/packs/eternal-garden-master-collection

I started browsing it and the loop featured in his song ‘Pain’ instantly grabbed my attention. I let my Intuition guide the writing process and before I knew it, I had a finished track on my hands. 

At the time I was meditating on relics.
Relics can be categorized as souvenirs with deep historical or personal value- often creating feelings of nostalgia or a reminder of experiences lost to the hands of time. Relics can also hold spiritual power and be used as a tool to strengthen or protect the holder.

The artwork features Suyat, an ancient writing script from the Philippines. Historically it was written on leaves and wood, but also carved into artifacts like pottery or jewelry. Using this script alongside the artwork is my way of re-imagining the relic as something that can live on-chain forever. Learning to write Suyat empowers me and I hope to share that feeling through the song and artwork.

Bianca Leonor Quiñones also known as QUIN is an independent multifaceted creator and musician based in Los Angeles. QUIN began by sharing her music through a style she describes as “Fantasy Soul” -A self made genre intended to showcase the power of boundless versatility through sound. Since then, Fantasy Soul has evolved into a world full of different creative mediums, events and experiences through the imagination of QUIN. 

*Thinkin Bout You II is a reimagined version of my original Thinkin Bout You Soundcloud release from 2015. My songs are often an open dialogue between me and my Highest Self. This is a love letter to me, a calling home after straying away too long; a conversation about dreaming my way back to Self.  

<3 Q

So after working with a publishing label that was treating me like I was a slave, I got stuck in form and this idea that songwriting has to be one way, I took some time to heal because I really couldn’t write for months. To help, I decided to ride my bike to clear my head, and one day I envisioned myself rapping a verse on the L.A. River. And that’s how “Joyride” came to life. 

“Joyride” is an evolving practice of free verses that are straight to it. No form, just me and me philosophies in bars. It’s a meditation, it’s short bits of me, it’s whatever you want to make it. An opportunity to just allow myself to ride the beat. To create these verses, I would start with a beat I love, rap on it and then send the accapella to Kaui to create something new out of it.

“Culture”, this first offering/verse off of “Joyride” came to me after rapping on Kaytranada’s production. I wrote the verse in a nite and immediately knew I didn’t want to add much else to it. I am very lyrical and I am realizing, sometimes one verse is enough. Sometimes keeping it simple is all you need. Sometimes just riding your own path is what I have to do. 

So this year as I’m riding my path, I guess I’m using this “Joyride” as an exercise in getting back to me, getting out of my way, sticking to my journey, continuing to create with bro Kaui who has been working with me for years, I’m really excited for how this ride will take me to more paths.  Next up “Showtime”

One of the toughest questions I’ve been asked in therapy was:

“How do you need people to show up for you?”

There have only been very few moments in my life where I’ve been lost for words and that probably lands in one of the top 3 moments. I truly did not have all the answers. I named a few things that I thought were “reasonable” and / or essential but my therapist pressed in more and said, “I didn’t ask what you thought was acceptable. I asked how you want people to show up for you.”

Prior to therapy, I was aware of some unhealthy habits I had picked up from my mother. I watched my mother on multiple occasions do so much for our family, so much for me growing up and so much for her friends that she would empty her cup at the drop a dime for people and not expect her cup to be filled in return by them. She did it out of pure love for people. 

But that caused her to be exhausted when she didn’t have to be. Sometimes too exhausted to do for herself in a personal way. 

In my course of healing and growing and raising the standard of what I expect from my friends, I remember getting into an argument with my wife about what I needed from her as one of my best friends. I remember telling her “I just don’t desire it…I need that from you.” 

Who knew that some self-discovery and an argument could give me all I needed to write this new record that I’m sure will encourage people to express what they need from their tribe.

For my genesis Sound drop it was important to stay true to the essence. I could’ve gone with another style of music but it was key for me to make history by sticking to the roots. When I first got into crypto in 2017, I noticed that the majority of the artists involved were in electronic music, a culture I was also a part of but I knew it would be an uphill battle to get Reggaeton recognition in the space. Fast-forward a few years and I accomplished everything I set out too in crypto/web3. (so far)

I made this song late 2021, I was on a hot streak knocking down about 3 records a night and “SOLTERA” was born. I needed a dope Reggaeton for the INFINXTE album and this was the one. The track is produced by two of my closest friends, Los Hitmen, a grammy-nominated production duo that have worked with heavyweights like J Balvin, Jay Wheeler, and De La Ghetto. I remember as soon as I sent the track I got a call back right away like “WTF DID YOU DO HERE?!” I knew right then we had a hit. 

The original artwork was crafted by one of my favorite artists from Spain, Diego (Paranoidme). I think one of the most exciting parts of my album is the diversity in collaborators, its completely organic and features artists from more than ten countries. Reggaeton was rejected in the mainstream for years and now its the voice of the youth all over Latin America, the Caribbean and people all over the world. Reggaeton pushes culture forward and I want to push it forward into web3.

22 years ago, I was on tour in Japan and in one of my favorite record stores in Tokyo crate digging. I struck up conversation with another crate digger who turned out to be Kabuki - and that started a whole new world of possibility. Pretty much on the spot, Kabuki asked me if I'd be interested in collaborating on a project and less than a year later I was in Germany in studio with him and his Megashira production partner Mainframe writing and recording their next album ('At Last'). Two whole decades later, we've reconnected with each other thanks to our shared passion for web3 - the power of blockchain!

This remix came into existence thanks to our first Mashibeats community remix contest, with finalists being chosen by our discord community and winners decided by $BUYBACK holders. Kabuki's remix was one of my personal favorites but didn't end up being in the final 4. Those 4 were minted as 1/1s on Catalog and now, today, we're celebrating the release of the remixes on vinyl (!) and very limited digital (no DSPs) with bonus tracks including this remix. To celebrate the vinyl release, Kabuki and I decided to share his amazing remix with the world via this Sound drop. 

The original of this track (a future drop?!) was my creative reaction to the summer of 2020 when we were in full lockdown, BLM was top of mind for the whole planet, which raised the perspective of [joy] as an act of [resistance] and how that sounds in my imagination. I'll leave it to Kabuki to tell us more about his remix:

"... when I heard "Joyful Resistance Part I" for the first time I fell in love with the chord progression: shades of modal Herbie and "Extensions"-era McCoy Tyner conjured a magical mood. I had to figure out how Mark did this! Once I worked out the harmonies I wrote an "answer" to Mark’s phrase, starting a musical conversation between the original and remix versions. 808 drums programmed in a jazz waltz pattern and my trademark ARP2600 synth bass provide the necessary contrast. Music that transcends all styles and traditions..." - Kabuki

zone out to the vibes with us... Joyful Resistance Part I remixed by Kabuki!

About "Nostalgia"

This piano piece arose from a few bars improvisation. I revisited this idea four years later and varied a little around it. Finally, in 2021, I completed the piece, which was then published in 2022. 

In finding a suitable title for this track and listening to it after a few days of absence, I realised it exuded nostalgic feel. The cover art aims to represent this nostalgic approach.
I remembered a silhouette of my profile created by a street paper cut artist in my childhood and felt this form of art would be a fitting choice. After familiarising myself with how to create paper cut art using a program for illustrations, I came up with a somewhat humorous take on the composition process -with me as the model. 

Adding a "paper cut like" artwork, the nostalgic thoughts about a childhood memory, and, of course, the vibe of the composition together was the final step for ´Nostalgia´.

The Golden Egg is a variation of the cover that incorporates the minting process -with the same whimsically smile of an older child.

SRA stands for “Source Recordings Augmentations”, product of the experimentation with audio that has been reshaped many times. It embraces Blockchain technology in the form of NFTs, setting a new standard in the way G89 Records releases music. By leveraging this approach, we can offer true digital ownership, ensure fair compensation for our artists, and streamline revenue distribution through smart contracts. NFTs also provide a unique way for fans to support our art, while reducing reliance on middlemen, increasing transparency. We believe this shift marks the next logical step in the evolution of the music and arts ecosystem, benefiting considerably all parties involved.

Art imitates life and life imitates art. Dreams are sacred and I believe we don’t quit until we’ve lived each one.

These are the words I want to say when I float away and leave my body behind. 

Time dissipates when I am dancing. My movement encapsulates the interconnectedness of memory, instinct, emotion, and truth. But when the sweat dries and the clocks start up again, my identity can become distorted and blurred. Regret, guilt, fear, and loss flood my mind, ripping me away from the love that colors my life.

This is disassociating for me; I am no longer in control of my body, words, or feelings and I am a shell with empty eyes. My mind hovers and every conversation is empty. My loved ones feel abandoned while we are sitting right across from one another. I wrote these lyrics while fighting a dissociative episode and I managed to come back to myself through making my experience tangible and real with words and sound.

This song is a reclamation of myself. When I’m ready to become real again, patient love is always there to welcome me back home.

"Cos the world that we're livin in -- 
kinda hard to be fittin in --

Angry Ape Society!"

In order to bring this whole vision to life, CREANS wanted to elevate both the music and the art to the same top-tier level. He wanted the art to be something people would WANT to collect so that meant he needed to partner up with someone truly great. This is where the magic and wonder of a perfect collaboration comes in. CREANS and ANGRY TENO knew each other through the AAS project and started having conversations about how to make the art contain the same freshness & energy that the song did, but also still be part of the Angry Apes Society's universe and lore. 

For CREANS, he wanted the artwork to not resemble a traditional album cover and instead be an actual collectible limited-edition NFT! In addition he also wanted the "Golden Egg" cover to be a completely different Angry Apes NFT, a true 1-of-1 Legendary Grail, raising the bar even higher for the collectors who love the exceptional art from ANGRY TENO and music from CREANS.

Everything being recorded in my bedroom with equipment I saved up for a slowly purchased along my music journey. Over the course of those years I was on a mission to once day get Dizzy Wright on one of my songs. Contacting his management multiple times and sending over song after song trying to make something work. 

After pounding the pavement long enough I found myself working on this song. Getting ready to release it, something felt like it was missing... 

So shooting my shot like any hungry artist would do, I sent the files to Dizzy's team and asked to give it a listen. 

After a couple days I got an email back saying he heard the track and he loved it. I went back to work on the song chopping it up so that there could be an open verse for Dizzy to work with. 

The rest was history. 

This song is proof that no matter who you are or how big your name is, Working hard and staying consistent will pay off.

Dive into the enchanting embrace of "Ocean Lullaby," a captivating 20 minute sound montage meticulously crafted from original field recordings I captured & processed over the course of 3 years, transcending the boundaries of conventional music composition. This auditory work ventures beyond the realms of traditional music, inviting contemplation with a thought-provoking question: What is music?

Immerse yourself in the gentle cadence of the sea as you embark on an ambient journey spanning three coastal states in America: Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina. "Ocean Lullaby" artfully weaves together a symphony of ocean waves and field recordings, creating an immersive soundscape that captures life on the coast.

For me, this conceptual soundwork challenges conventional notions of music, encouraging you as the listeners to ponder the essence of melody, rhythm, and harmony. Is music confined to traditional instruments and structured compositions, or can it be found in the symphony of the natural world? "Ocean Lullaby" invites you to explore these questions as you listen.

This piece of audio can serve as a soothing backdrop for various activities or moments of reflection. Whether you're looking for a serene soundscape to enhance relaxation & meditation, or simply looking for a calming ambience while working, reading, or unwinding for the day, "Ocean Lullaby" can provide that for you. The gentle ebb and flow of ocean waves, coupled with layers of field recordings, can transport you to the coastal states of Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina, allowing you to find peace and focus amidst the chaos of our modern lives. 

With "Ocean Lullaby", you're invited to experience the allure of the ocean's embrace and embark on a contemplative journey that transcends the boundaries of sound. It's not just a song; it's an invitation to join me in redefining the very essence of music itself.

The Beaver Jam Club is the musicians' collective focused on cutting edge music production, founded by Brandon Schroeder. What began as an interview on the Beaver Jam Club's Artist Spotlight show, episode #4 on Twitter (X) Spaces, now available on podcast streaming platforms, blossomed into a creative friendship. Brandon had a vision to create a song based on the amazing freestyle Rohan did with the infamous loop "I Got 5 On It." The song envisioned was to be inspired by the tougher, true-to-life golden era hip hop classics contrasted by the spirit-filled, melodious vocals of reggae music. Brandon teamed up with his brother Ryan and they created the music heard on the track today. Ryan Schroeder is an amazingly talented musician and was crucial in the genesis of this track with Brandon. The song was then sent to Rohan with the help of his manager @$MoneyLoooong$ on Twitter (X). Vocals were recorded by RDG at G.L.O.W. Entertainment studios in North Carolina, US in July, 2023. When finished with many electrifying takes, the recordings were sent to @MerkleyMusic on Twitter (X) with Christopher Merkley for the mixing and mastering. The final production was done between everyone involved including: Brandon Schroeder, Ryan Schroeder, Rohan Da Great, and Christopher Merkley, however none of the production for this song could have been done without the genius of Christopher Merkley's mixing abilities. Brandon is honored to have been able to work with so many truly talented artists to bring this vision to fruition. By minting this song, "Greatness Indeed," you support independent musicians who strive to survive in a world that doesn't appreciate them nearly to the extent it use to. Streaming platforms are nearly impossible to make a decent living on alone and the expectations for what a new album release can bring-in financially are marginal compared to the amounts seen just a couple decades ago. Now with the advent of blockchain tech and smart contracts, the power can be given back to the music creators as opposed to the hand's of big business. A new landscape is being built on the revolutionary minds of web3 devs, paving the way with unique and exciting ways to connect, grow, and remain independent as a musician.

The values of web3 align with Rohan Da Great's mission to support independent music and the culture of music NFTs is what inspired him to get involved, support other artists, and begin creating in this space. This is far from a one time venture for Rohan as he is already in the works collabing with other NFT projects and finding anyway he can to participate, give-back, and to grow alongside the rest of the web3 music family at large.

Rohan Da Great, son of legendary dancehall artist Curry Don, is an aspiring MC hailing from east Flatbush Brooklyn New York now residing in North Carolina. RDG is driven by one goal; to administer great music to the world. With his L.A.R. Entertainment (Leaders of the Artist Revolution) Imprint, his versatility, exceptional bar delivery and ear for music, Rohan sets himself apart from the upcoming class of MC's. Previous releases such as “Rule The World” & "Say Goodbye" have tested the waters and came out on top with flying colors. Since their release the songs have been featured on multiple major blogs, radio stations and several magazines which have all sang the praise of the breath of fresh air that is Rohan Da Great. The songs were able to touch people and evoke emotions and ideals that made them reminisce on the past and contemplate creating a better future. Nowadays versatility within independence is the key to any successful artist and Rohan Da Great exemplifies those traits. We’ve seen plenty of rappers pay homage to, and dabble in the Dancehall/Reggae genre, but not many artists can switch genres completely and still hold their own. It seems as though many artists are incapable of finding that elusive sweet spot in their artistry to deliver on both spectrums.

Rising Dancehall star RDG, more recently known for his chart-topping releases like “Fallin’,” and “Unfair Games,” which made it to #1 on iTunes and the Top 100 on Urban Radio respectively, has cracked the code. Rohan had a promising rap career with releases, but somewhere along the line he decided to switch it up and it worked effortlessly.

He just expanded his reach with the newly released track, "She Single" and then the longly anticipated collab song with the Beaver Jam Club "Greatness Indeed." Armed with an unmatched level of versatility, lyrical prowess, an ear for catchy beats and an unrivaled work ethic, Rohan Da Great is sure to reach international levels of success and will undoubtedly be a household name in the years to come.

- I moved to Nashville in 2016 with my girlfriend I'd been with for 4 years. She got a job as an E.R. nurse, I came to pursue music. We moved into a two-bedroom apartment together and life was great. I was chasing my dreams and lived with the woman that I planned on spending my life with. After a few years without having any real success as an artist/songwriter, she asked me one day after a long stressful shift at the hospital, "How long are you going to chase this for?" I answered "as long as it takes"... which was and still is my truth.
- After that conversation everything changed. She changed. She wanted security, and I wasn't it. Our relationship started to suffer. That's when Baltimore called. She got offered a 3 month travel nursing assignment to move to Baltimore. She would be able to pay off her student loans and it would also give us a little space, maybe just what we needed.
- A few weeks later she packed up her car, gave me a kiss goodbye, and headed off to Baltimore. Little did I know that it would be the last time we would kiss, and the last time I would see her. After she got there, she didn't answer my texts or calls. Our relationship was over. It became clear that she had made her decision to end our relationship before she left Nashville and that maybe this was the most pain-free way of doing it. I was heartbroken, she was my first true love and it hurt to lose her. I wanted to hate her for it, but I couldn't. This life I have chosen as a troubadour is not for everyone, and It just wasn't for her. I wanted her to find happiness, even if it wasn't with me... and that is what inspired this song, "Baltimore"
- For anyone who has ever been with someone who left them without warning... I present to you... "Baltimore".

This song took more than a decade to manifest. This song's surrealistic lyrics and haunting verse melodies were born from a whiskey-fueled dream about a non-sensical conversation in a dark western bar after an ordinary night out in 2010. Luckily, the dreamer woke up with enough sense to realize the potential of this little dream diddy and immediately recorded what he remembered into his iPhone while in bed. Initial drafts of a fuller song with a chorus and bridge were soon written and recorded in the hopes of something sticking, but nothing ever did. Frustrated, the dreamer dropped the diddy and moved on with life...

Fast forward ten years later, and the dreamer woke again from a dream, floating among white, snow-capped mountains with a curious melody blaring in the sky. It was a dream that felt vaguely familiar. Drifting back into consciousness, the dreamer realized it was the continuation of that conversation from that dark Western bar. It was the same dream -- only a proper chorus was born this time. La Cita jams on this concept soon and then ensues, where the song is fully fleshed out and elevated into its current form. 

Like most things, finding meaning, connecting the dots, and looking forward are hardly natural. Sometimes, a dream doesn't end when you wake up; sometimes, it takes more than 10 years to complete a feeling. But looking back, this song is heavily influenced by a love of Spaghetti Western movies and dancing to cumbia music in dark bars. It honors the slow, mysterious, and often aimless character arc from a good Western we go through before seeing things more clearly from a higher vantage point. And yet it leaves room for the mystery and longing that often remain...

He looked me dead in the eye as he sat up and grabbed my arm, his seriousness taking me aback. The whole scene really. His eyes a bit cold. His large and ever-commanding frame, frailed by time.

He was on his deathbed and we both knew it. 

There were times when we didn’t know what to do - when I didn’t know what to do - except sit. Except think that a young man ought to be near his grandfather during his final days on earth. 

He was not a vulnerable man, Paw Paw. Charming, yes, a smile that could melt your heart or bend your will *just so* whether you were part of the family or had just met. But vulnerable, no.

So when he looked at me - as he broke the silence that we had been sitting in for hours that turned into days that turned into weeks that turned into the passing of a generation - when he looked at me and broke that silence - to tell me a quip that crossed his mind or why he thought Nicholas Cage was great in Raising Arizona - every bit of small talk was like - have i spent my whole life really not getting to know you? not asking a single question beyond what i could see? and when he broke the silence…

“I coulda been a singer.”

Stunned, having been lost in my own world, contemplating the silence and sitting and sitting and - stunned.

“But you were, Paw Paw, you *are*.” My heart careful not to place his life in the past tense. “You have a gold medal in singing - in chorus competition - the barbershop society - a gold medal -“ my voice raising in pitch as my heartbeat quickened, pleading to the moment, “the quartets - your quartet - the spellbinders - you were a singer, you ARE - “

“No.” 

He interrupted deeply, but kindly. 

Stolidly, with his full self, he spoke again.

“Like Sinatra.” 

So matter-of-fact.

He lay back - his strong-broad-frail shoulders lay back as the life he imagined flashed before my eyes - the crowds lost in ecstasy swaying in unison, the dancing lights reflecting through the sweat dripping from the brows of the great entertainer, the bathed in gold, the showing up to play your role, the diamonds, the sparkling eyes, the grit and glamour of a public life.

Once more from the silence:

“If you really want to be famous, change your name to Sky Bravo.”

He looked me dead in the eye as he sat up and grabbed my arm, his seriousness taking me aback. The whole scene really. His eyes a bit cold. His large and ever-commanding frame, frailed by time.

He was on his deathbed and we both knew it.

“show me” was a really fun song to make, and the creative process from start to finish was unlike anything I had made before. When I first made this track, what is now the verse was actually the “drop” or the main hook, the song was much slower, and I had written and recorded my own vocals on it. It was a cool track, but I knew it could be better (i'm not a very good singer). That's when I decided to send the instrumental to a songwriter and vocalist, with no instruction other than to “have fun with it” and see what she could do. I absolutely loved what she sent back and I ended up making two different new versions of the song. I made one version with the original drop and her new vocals layered over the top, which made a sort of Nu Disco Indie-Electronic track. The second version I made was a high-energy bass house drop that used all of the ad libs she recorded and some bouncy bass lines I had written underneath them. In the end, I took both ideas and was able to mold them into one track to get the best of both worlds, and that's the tune you hear today. Hope you enjoy dancing to this one as much as I did making it! see you soon. - informal.

I’m Upper Reality, producer and artist, and I have been developing myself for 10 years.  As a longtime creator, I have grown and changed immensely and watched the industry do the same.  “Rise,” is a reimagining of the exhilaration, appreciation, joy, pain, and ultimately, exhaustion, that I have garnered following this life path.

I have an Economics degree from the University of Texas at Austin.  I used to not mention it, because it didn’t seem “cool,” but the more I traversed my journey, the more I began to see how cliques, identities, buzzwords, and other superficial considerations go into valuation of a person and what they do.  This understanding has led me to have a more active, intellectual role in my work, just in time for the intersection of music and fintech to make a place for it.  There is a sociological and spiritual revolution happening with my work that I seek for all listeners to feel and understand when they listen to what I’m creating.  This is all my production, all my music theory understanding, all my vocal training, all my Ableton practice, and all of the closed doors that have never recognized what I have felt to be a gift that I have.  See, “Rise,” is not just about a vacant, toxic-positive chant to peace and love—it is a proverbial snatching of the goalpost—a declaration of “sleep on me, I’ll sleep on you,” to all of the times that I have had my core wounds invoked by organizations, groups, systems, and people, that I wanted to value me, accept me, etc. only to be rejected, humiliated, abandoned for superficial reasons, yet told it’s something that I’m lacking.  “Rise” says “Nope, I was never the problem.  And now, with the joys I reach on my own terms, you all will see that, from afar.”

I am at a point of detachment to the outcome, as to whether or not I will be heard, recognized, celebrated, or valued.  As of now, this is just a special piece, that means a lot to me, and means a lot that the Sound audience would be keen to listen.  I enjoy the piece very deeply, but I have left it in it’s raw, early stages, before tweaking it to see whether DSP’s will bite. So this is a special, limited edition, that won’t be released anywhere else.

For more information of the entire context of what I’m wanting to do in Web3, please check out my proposal video:

Darby and I had been discussing the healing journey, and how someone (or something) can leave a void in your life after they're gone. This echo can't be moved on from until you confront your past. Sonically, we wanted this track to be layered with texture and ambience, and have chords that gave you the feeling of that emotional tug of war. Clover's speech (the spoken word intro) represents the resolution to this- that you need to make peace with your past in order to move forward and heal. Our goal was to make something that would uplift and inspire people going through similar struggles.

Nvak Collective is a next-generation record label and artist advocacy collective that fully embraces web3 to uplift creators. Our mission is to build a more equitable, profitable, and diverse music industry that puts the underrepresented first, recognizing that the current system is in need of major disruption. Our small team has already discovered talent from remote regions around the globe and launched them to billions of streams and hundreds of thousands of fans, all while providing artist-friendly deals and artist care. 

With a focus on signing and developing women, non-binary, and LGBTQ+ artists from emerging markets, we see web3 as a tool to better help these creators tell their stories, earn new revenue streams, and connect with their biggest fans. Since June of 2022, we’ve worked hard to bring rising artists such as Annika Rose into the web3 space, and will continue to bridge the gap in web3 education and onboarding for artists seeking to take the leap.

She became the first artist signed to Nvak Collective in 2020, and has since surpassed over 1 billion streams and will be opening up tours for Ed Sheeran, Young the Giant & Milky Chance this summer 2023.

"Don't Take Your Love" was released on May 22, 2020, roughly two months after "15 days to slow the spread". It was my last release of 2020 and my final solo/pop track before fully entering the EDM space in 2021. 

The song first came to life while I was messing with a vocal plugin I recently purchased and experimenting with stacking a lot of vocals together to make a choir/gang vocal. The line that started that experiment was, "No, don't take your love from me." 

The lyrics were inspired by a relationship on the verge of collapse, and the feelings of experiencing someone's love slowly fade. It's interesting and kind of poetic, though, that the song lyrics are beautifully and tragically paralleled with the love of the world gradually being replaced by fear. So I'd say "Don't Take Your Love" is also a song about the desperate plea to not lose love in the world during one of the most extraordinary times of our lives. 

"Don't Take Your Love" is one of the few songs in my career that is 100% written, recorded, produced, mixed, and mastered entirely by myself. This style of song is the kind of music I want to return to making in the future. 

This Music NFT release with Sound is a brand new endeavor for me in the Web3 space, so a massive thank you to them for reaching out and another huge thank you to everyone who mints this song. 

From the bottom of my heart, it really does mean the world to me when anyone finds a connection with something I've created. 

Much Love and God bless, 

Zack Gray

In honor of Pride Month “Freedom Bass” is a celebration of the radical and connective power of dance music. A disco-house track and call-to-arms for the queer and dance communities alike. 

A nostalgic, yet forward-thinking track, “Freedom Bass” a lyrical call to action for resistance and change set against a mashup of disco and 90’s house. Written during the pandemic, in the heart of lockdown, the song is filled with melancholy and a desire to return to the dance floor, surrounded by joyful crowds and uninhibited self-expression. 

“Freedom Bass was the first song that we ever wrote together in the basement of Boy Untitled's LA home during quarantine. This was long before we decided to become a boy band (lol) and like most first sessions, we were just feeling each other out to see if we would catch a vibe. We put the track down only to return to it a year later. Little did we know that this would become the thesis of BOY2K: 'The dance floor is the revolution...this is Music For The People.' Our mission as artists is to create spaces for people to come back "home" to. Spaces to find ourselves. Spaces to connect. Space to riot against systems of oppressions. Spaces to imagine the new world that we want to create together."

BOY2K’s mission is to make “Music For The People,” that is, music that celebrates the power of community. A community built in mutual support, love, acceptance and music that begs the listener to get up and move!

Learn more about BOY2K at www.boy2k.com.

“CUFFED”  - one of the four singles leading up to my sophomore album “ANGEL OF SADNESS”, self produced and written by me. The whole project is a set of love songs, not only to people but to my head and heart.

Pt. 5/5 (Answers EP)

‘Answers’ came to me unexpectedly one summer morning at 2 am. I was in a trance, playing the chords repeatedly until the lyrics seemed to write themselves. It felt like the words were given to me before I fully understood them. At that time, I had been reflecting on the idea that our reality could be part of a grand experiment, a giant holographic pulse. Everything I was reading and listening to seemed to hint at this concept. The purpose being to disconnect us from the truth of who we are, through the limitations of the human body, societal programming, and cycles of suffering, to see if we remember. But what do we remember? I believe the answer can never be expressed in words. It's a felt sense that we all glimpse from time to time. At the deepest level, I think we have all, at a soul level, agreed to be part of this game, not to seek escape, but to fully immerse ourselves in every facet of it, knowing that it is, in fact, just a game.

Uffie is the project of the globe-trotting artist and fashion icon Anna-Catherine Hartley, formerly signed to Ed Banger Records, where she became acquainted with legendary producers of the early 2000s French electronic music scene. Her career spanned many successes including her first viral hit song called “Pop The Glock,” which was originally posted on MySpace and launched her fame in the Bloghouse era of dance music. She collaborated with the French electronic duo Justice on “TThhEe PPaARRtTYY,” which appeared on their Grammy nominated album Cross in 2007. Her debut album, Sex Dreams and Denim Jeans, was nominated at the French Victoires de la Musique for Best Electronic Album in 2010. She has since collaborated with Pharrell Williams, Charli XCX, Galantis, and Mr. Oizo, to name a few. 

Uffie returned in 2018 with her debut single “Drugs” from her EP Tokyo Love Hotel. A muse to the art world, she collaborated with Jam Sutton in 2019 on a marble statue and A.I. experience, accompanied by her track “Ego.” She is currently writing for other artists, with credits including Pink, Khalid, Greyson Chance, Blu DeTiger, VINCINT, and Tegan & Sara. Her sophomore full-length, Sunshine Factory, was executive produced by Toro y Moi and released last spring on his label Company Records. You can hear her writing and vocals featured on The Blessed Madonna’s comeback single this past November titled “Serotonin Moonbeams.”  

For Uffie’s first official NFT drop, she chose to bring one of her favorite unreleased songs to life. “Babydoll” was created with longtime collaborators Lokoy and Veronika Jane Wyman (of DAGR). What began as a poem on a calm quiet morning, ended as a ketamine-inspired freestyle. Enjoy the ride.

“Illegal Rave Tapes” is the first ever wax treatment for Acrelid, courtesy of Dance Data Records. Originally comprised of 134 tracks, this distilled collection is a snapshot of John Lee Richardson’s archive of music from between 1999-2012.

Since the ripe age of 12, he’s been drawing inspiration from the UK rave scene in the 90’s that he found himself in. That spark was the beginning of a lifelong obsession. He set out to capture the essence of what he felt and saw surrounding him during that time; whether it was via recording loops out of a playstation 1 to cassette / CD or borrowing any other gear he could get his hands on / that people would lend him.

What’s less important than all the gear he used are the sounds he captured with them. “Sinister beats” that all share a driving quality of rhythm, spanning across smudged influences from jungle to acid and the BBC Radiophonic Workshop transmissions. It’s clear from the tunes that this is someone who’s clocked 1000’s of hours tinkering and refining his sound, and who has squeezed every function out of his machines, just for the fun of it all. Having seldom released music since the 90’s, John’s been waiting for the right moment to share it with the world, and this collection has very much been worth the wait.

Corrosiv, the sophomore album from Orchestroll, reveals the duo at their most mature and vulnerable. Originally conceived as a reflection on hybridity and bastardization, the album deploys New Age and ambient compositional tropes as a launchpad, exposing their trite sanctity to the realities of corrosion. Having come of age in the 1970s and 1980s, the New Age movement perdures today as a domain of contradictions; its promise of transcendence riddled with the very commercialized dogma from which its adherents claim to flee. Healing modalities such as reiki, crystal therapy, and sound baths are simultaneously pathways to solace and sites of exploitation; their sonic counterparts — ethereal synth pads, shimmering textures, celestial drones — claim to facilitate meditation and enlightenment while devolving into empty signifiers of vitality. With Corrosiv, Orchestroll displays neither reverence nor disdain toward New Age: they exhume it instead, revealing the saccharine effervescence and commodified murk undergirding its aesthetics. The result is intoxicating — disquieting.

As most of us now live in a world saturated with information, this album feels like a reflection of how the modern world might sound if it were to process its own chaos through a unified scream. Hailing from the highlands of Bandung, West Java, a city where tradition and modernization intertwine in the rhythm of daily life, Xin Lie unpretentiously translates this cultural fusion into a sonically rich and rhythmically bold debut LP.

The artist’s roots in the hardcore and punk scenes reverberate throughout the album, though they’ve been reshaped and refined for the club. There’s an undeniable pleasure in experiencing the chaos Xin Lie channels—irregular beats, dynamic frequencies, and disjointed grooves collide and expand, each track laced with a sense of unpredictable energy. Yet even in its most chaotic moments, the music feels deliberate, its edges softened by a sense of compositional care.

The album reveals a strange duality: tracks that seem to beckon you to the dance floor but never quite let you settle there. Frequencies flicker and fluctuate in patterns that feel just slightly off-grid, as though resisting traditional structures. Yet, amidst the digital textures, Xin Lie weaves in organic sounds—snippets of native conversations or environmental noise—creating layers that feel both intimate and expansive.It’s fair to say this album extends far beyond the boundaries of today’s club music.

Corrosiv, the sophomore album from Orchestroll, reveals the duo at their most mature and vulnerable. Originally conceived as a reflection on hybridity and bastardization, the album deploys New Age and ambient compositional tropes as a launchpad, exposing their trite sanctity to the realities of corrosion. Having come of age in the 1970s and 1980s, the New Age movement perdures today as a domain of contradictions; its promise of transcendence riddled with the very commercialized dogma from which its adherents claim to flee. Healing modalities such as reiki, crystal therapy, and sound baths are simultaneously pathways to solace and sites of exploitation; their sonic counterparts — ethereal synth pads, shimmering textures, celestial drones — claim to facilitate meditation and enlightenment while devolving into empty signifiers of vitality. With Corrosiv, Orchestroll displays neither reverence nor disdain toward New Age: they exhume it instead, revealing the saccharine effervescence and commodified murk undergirding its aesthetics. The result is intoxicating — disquieting.

The union between Indian sound system ballistics, Bay Area’s industrial resistance ethos, and feral soundscapes personifies “Timeslave III”. Only Now splits this hour long escapade into molten drum exercises and dripping melancholic instrumentals, littered with traditional Hindustani instruments and Punjabi synth gymnastics. Alternating fluidly between hyperkinetic drumwork and sweeping, contemplative electronic music, Arora produces an album which is vast and unremittingly abrasive yet deceptively intimate and inextricably tied to his origins.

With a nod to the current soundclash/dhol tasha phenomena throughout India, things come full circle with Kush’s forward vision from years past and current states of his homeland’s soundsystem obsessions. Built upon years of warped percussion workouts, punjabi drone swamps, and Arora’s legacy of taking his roots to extremes, 2025 celebrates 10 years since Only Now’s first EP. Guest appearances from Argentina’s Jaijiu, percussionist Dave Sharma, and Kolkata’s Shubho Sharma form center pieces in the different seasons of the record as it waxes from seething to withdrawn.

All the tracks were performed, road tested throughout a period of a year of shows in the US, UK, Japan, and then brought into the studio in the latter part of 2024 for mixing and arrangement.

Low Recordings presents its latest EP, a 12” with two definitive sides recorded by underground fog dwellers, Earth Boys.

Michael Sherburn and Julian Duron’s 15th release is a quintessential eBoys listening experience, where headphones, car stereos and club systems are created equal.

’Cold World E.P.’ gets right to the point with moody locked synth grooves and warm tape noise between two uncomplicated, almost stark melodies, giving any true fan a familiar feeling.

Drums take a back seat, heavy leads swell and vocal samples leap right out of the discount bin—as they always have—Earth Boys maintain a conscious balance between deep feeling, focused production and fun.

Title track ‘Cold World’ is a swirling, ghostly nose dive, with punchy bass hits and an odd looping arrangement designed to get listeners in the zone. A2 ‘Sad Boys’ is a casual, nonchalant, head bobbing drum loop that weaves though Earth Boys’ typical holy trinity of chiller sounds—soft leads, wind instruments and deep bass.

Side B kicks in the doors of the club starting off with ‘In The House’, a subtle yet massive 909 assault, with hard hats, hazy synths and a vintage rolling bass line. ‘Feel So Good’ is another dip into the rich lineage of Earth Boys’ more candy coated tracks such as LSD, I Just Love It, and Be Happy With Who You Are—a proper dance floor number. Let's also not forget the smooth remix that detroit legend, Rick Wade, throws down.

Overall the EP feels like a brief survey of the New York producers’ musical repertoire, another day, another eBoys record, but as always, freshly rolled joints just hit a little different.

In this latest release, Rick delves into the depths of his soul to create a truly soulful sound. The EP opens with "Lonely Expedition," a track that begins with gentle yet poignant keys and expansive sounds, creating a sense of calm while building anticipation. As the track progresses, the smooth kick drums kick in, paving the way for the rest of the expedition with a familiar, heartwarming groove.

The following track, "My Soul," is a deeply evocative piece that features haunting vocals and captivating samples from classic films, all interwoven with a pulsating kick drum that underscores the profound journey of the soul. The EP comes to a close with "The Emperor," a steady ascent out of the soul with its ethereal beats, melancholic chords, and mellow baseline. The addition of a heartwarming sample from Charlie Chaplin's "The Great Dictator" adds a revitalizing touch to this beautiful and moving track.

Overall, Rick has delivered an exceptional EP that showcases his unique talents and creativity. The sounds of his soul are sure to captivate and delight listeners, leaving them feeling energized and inspired

Michigan-born Rick Wade might not get the headlines of his more celebrated Detroit peers, but few have done as much to contribute to the house canon as he. For nearly three decades, Wade has consistently turned out deeply channeled grooves, utilizing every second of their often-elongated lengths. Peppered lightly with strings, an odd breathy voice or some other delicate hook culled from the funk and soul sounds of his youth, Wade's style is the perfect embodiment of minimalist production delivering maximum impact.

The Brussels-based Algerian DJ and producer serves up five cuts of percussive club music inspired by traditional Berber music and British sound system culture. It’s a winning combo that will delight fans of the likes of DJ Plead, Toumba and the Livity Sound catalogue. It’s all deliciously minimal, with playful chirrups of bass, melody, and buoyant drums woven seamlessly around technoid pulses. From the lower tempos on display in ‘BubbleFly’, ‘Bull Run’ and ‘Smooth Jump’ to the nimbler flexes of ‘Baraka’ and ‘Siwtchover’, it’s an EP that displays the producer’s knack for subtly bubbling beats and mood-setting dancefloor NRG.

"Rain from Heaven’s debut album, "petra-coeur", brings listeners into a vast liminal dreamspace between genres, one that is both pulsing with mystery and strangely familiar. Weaving together lush tapestries of guitar, gently danceable electro-acoustic beats, and warm ambient soundscapes, "petra-coeur" shimmers around Vazquez’s singularly nimble and yearning vocals, anchored all the while by an earthy post-grunge undercurrent. 

Nature, in all its forms and complexities, is the protagonist of "petra-coeur". Here, the digital and the organic blur into stunning new configurations, as Vazquez ruminates on urbanized indigeneity, ecological disaster, and love’s radical capacity for healing and regeneration. " -Kerosene Jones

The Brussels-based Algerian DJ and producer serves up five cuts of percussive club music inspired by traditional Berber music and British sound system culture. It’s a winning combo that will delight fans of the likes of DJ Plead, Toumba and the Livity Sound catalogue. It’s all deliciously minimal, with playful chirrups of bass, melody, and buoyant drums woven seamlessly around technoid pulses. From the lower tempos on display in ‘BubbleFly’, ‘Bull Run’ and ‘Smooth Jump’ to the nimbler flexes of ‘Baraka’ and ‘Siwtchover’, it’s an EP that displays the producer’s knack for subtly bubbling beats and mood-setting dancefloor NRG.

Words by EOIN MURRAY.

Kamoun has developed a signature sound where percussive intensity meets atmospheric depth, blending polyrhythmic drums with modern electronic textures. His fascination for traditional tribal percussion, paired with influences from minimalist field recordings and British bass culture, generates a hypnotic energy that resonates with the raw power of contemporary electronic music.
With the Artefact EP, Kamoun unveils three tracks exploring diverse sonic landscapes. Each piece stands out with its own identity, where rich vocals & textures and rhythmic complexity meet unexpected twists. There's something unpredictable that always surprises us that keeps the listener captivated from start to finish.

Ah, Byron, Byron, Byron—what can we say? We're absolutely enamored with this guy's music. And, we couldn't be more thrilled to welcome him into our family on Low Recordings.

We are back with our second vinyl release, featuring Byron's "Love 4 Music." This 4-track EP is a celebration of love, with Side A and Side B showcasing two distinct styles where Byron truly shines. Side A delivers the club hits, while Side B envelops us in a soulful/R&B/deep house vibe.

Kicking off Side A is "Creepin' With U." The track begins with haunting chords that exude an eerie and raw vibe, swiftly leading into a thumping, club-certified kick drum. As the song progresses, a hint of nostalgia from the lo-fi days creeps in, complemented by vocal samples that add to the eerie atmosphere. Yes, it's eerie, but it's also robust and captivating—perfect for enticing bodies to move on a warehouse dance floor.

Next up is "Work That Girl (Tribal Mix)," the heavyweight of the four, tailor-made for the club/warehouse scene. The track starts with the clicking and clacking of hats and snares, Byron's vocals weaving in and out of the mix. The lyrics are crafted for a sweaty night of dancing, and as the kicks thump in, the energy rises. Byron's trademark chords seamlessly ooze into the mix, uniting our bodies with the song. Acid-sounding notes eventually lead us in and out of the groove—a solid club anthem.

Flipping over to Side B, we're greeted by "Inner Visions," where Byron slows things down and takes us in a different direction. A classic synth line initiates the track with a smooth kick, creating an airy vibe that melds perfectly with its melody. As the song grooves, Byron's soulful vocals pierce through, infusing warmth into his words. The warmth persists as the song progresses, with his voice echoing slightly more dissonance, leaving us with a proper vision for the closing track.

Closing out the EP, Byron guides us with a vision for a fun night in "Make Me Feel." Deep with a touch of R&B, the song exudes warmth and is all about feeling good with the person who got you through the night. Byron's sultry voice sits perfectly on the track as the basslines guide us through. His playful nature keeps things light and fun, rounding off the EP on a high note.

Seven months have slipped by. No sleep‑scribbled letters, no words from the Council. After releasing Vol. 1, I thought I’d feel relief, even freedom to make new stuff—but all I felt was a ghostly insistence—as if there were a chore I had to complete first, something I’d forgotten about. I began treating that absence as a puzzle. What was it trying to show me? I pride myself on keeping things tidy—yet like any producer, I keep a graveyard of musical ideas. While poking around my hard drive, I stumbled on a couple of tracks set aside during the making of A Spectral Turn. Could that be it? Maybe they were just waiting for their moment.

So, for Volume 2, I’ve gathered those pieces—some sketched in studio sessions three years ago, others composed for my live‑sets that followed the album release.

"Healing Out Loud" is a groundbreaking musical experience from Heno. + Mad Keys that encourages listeners to confront their vulnerabilities and share their stories. This project redefines what it means to heal, grow, & connect with others by openly sharing the genuine truths of our human experiences. 

Heno. tells a story of personal growth, resilience, & the profound strength in embracing the scars that make us unique. Mad Keys provides a diverse sonic landscape with stylings tailored to amplify the emotions & stories shared by Heno. The project takes listeners on an introspective journey that's both personal & universal, fostering connection & understanding. 

This 10-track album is currently being mixed & mastered by Gregory Ebert, with creative direction from Karim Ali, content creation from Jamee Cornelia & features from MoRuf & Jaszy Shavers.

Éditions Appærent and Pierre Guerineau are proud to present L’eau par la soif, their shared debut record.

Named after historical cases of mass hallucinations in French villages, Feu St-Antoine’s music reflects the subjectivity of reality, both as a personal and socio-political construct.

From the cold vocoder of “The Appærence” to the phased, swirling rhythms of “Spazio Libero,” or the vast, sprawling synth epics “L’eau par la soif” and “Printemps,” this record is immaculately rendered at every level; suffused with thoughts half-remembered, emotions never felt, and languages unlearned.

Language plays a crucial role here. Monologues and snatched phrases are buried in these tracks; one can even detect the cry and speech of Alex Zhang Hungtai’s slabbed, event-horizon saxophone. “L’eau par la soif” traverses the space between what is known and unknown, what is felt and unfelt, what is true and what is merely fact.

A few weeks ago, I woke up in bed to find a letter in my own handwriting

The Assembly of Many Names, duly convened and vested with authority across dimensions, hereby declares, as a matter of immutable principle, that tracks imbued with the memory of motion must not be confined or withheld. Such works, herein referred to as 'dance tracks,' are to spill freely into shadowed rooms, loud, unhindered and unbound. The practice of gatekeeping shall henceforth be abolished."

This could only mean one thing: it’s time to put together a new EP series. Starting with some tracks inspired by Tokyo's dancefloors I got to experience last summer. The next volumes will follow in their own time—every few months if I can keep up. I wouldn’t dare to challenge the Assembly.

Spectral Bounce proudly presents Zevar, the debut release by Aedis, an alias of David Iriarte. This new undertaking sees the Amsterdam-based artist plumbing the depths & tunnelling further into a sound that has surely been in the works for some time. One half of Iro Aka, Iriarte is no stranger to the exploration of ambiance & rhythmic play: the duo released a trilogy of records on John Talabot’s label Hivern Discs between 2020 & 2023.

On Zevar, Iriarte first traverses the deeper territories of tech house before conjuring up mystic 2-step and delving into rolling techno. The sense of spaciousness throughout the EP is vivid: perpetually unfolding modulated delays; cavernous reverb; weighty, grounding sub frequencies. This expanse is punctuated by fragmentary voices, psychedelic refrains (“Xtz”), intricate break deployment (“Station”) and thudding bass tones (“RTHM”). Just enough is given, just enough held back. With these 4 tracks, Aedis brings you that little bit deeper.

Art by Susanne Janssen
Words by Cameron Leaf

Reflex Blue debuts on Spectral Bounce with The Bleeps, a five-track EP that weaves a somber yet captivating late-night ambiance. Over a string of releases in recent years, Reflex Blue has been sculpting a distinct and evolving sound, blending the core minimal aesthetic of UK Tech House with influences from his homeland.

This homage to early 2000's Tech House captures its essence while infusing it with a fresh, pulsating perspective. The opening track, 'Dracula’s MPC', sets the tone with its club-ready elements: crisp drums, deep bass lines, and captivating vocal samples that command attention throughout. On the B-side, "Interlude" offers a glimpse into Reflex Blue’s large palette with its boppy and quirky breaks. It's a spectral record in every sense, making it the perfect sophomore release for the label.

Written and produced by Cooper Fraser
Artwork by Susanne Janssen
Words by Hervé Kacou

Through their music curation work at One Eye Witness, co-founder Hylke has been silently influencing the sounds that resonate in clubs and underground dance music record collections around the world.

His newly created label Spectral Bounce takes it one step deeper, providing a platform for music imbued with eerie grooves and subtly expressive energy, capturing the listener right at their core.

SPEC01 - Force of Nature - Is the fruit of the long-standing musical relationship and shared visions of producer and Selector RDS and Spectral Bounce, the perfect catalogue opener.

Over four moody club-ready tracks, RDS dives into the sound of the after-hours, where minds are freed and darker energies are expressed. Both sides display perfectly controlled acid synthesis, heart-grabbing bass lines, cut-through drum sampling and an extremely textured and gritty mix. RDS' musical influences are clearly felt, harmoniously fusing UK 90s bleep techno, spacey tech house and dub with his own emotional perspective to club music.

The Dutch producer's distinct dance floor sound is here captured in its essence, processed through his expressive electronic machines while controlling tempo and energy in a unique manner. This EP is a sonic statement, offering the listener the Spectral Bounce sound.

Words by Hervé Kacou
Artwork & Logo by Susanne Janssen

DDR004 is "Mapagkeun Kawani," the debut 12" EP from Bandung’s own Xin Lie. This three-track offering skillfully combines the ethos of Bandung's hardcore punk scene with the evocative rhythms of Sundanese Dogdog drums, crafting a sound that is reflective of Xin Lie’s diverse musical background and connection to Indonesia's musical history.

Xin Lie, born Diannov Pamungkas, has navigated multiple worlds, starting from his days in the hardcore punk scene to exploring the traditional performing arts of his Sundanese heritage. This journey informs his approach to production, particularly his use of traditional percussion which he samples and recontextualizes into a modern electronic drum palette.

The EP includes two remixes: producer Bagvs delivers a sharp, stripped-down take on "MAPAGKEUN," while New York's Laenz transforms "PANEN" into a fast-paced, percussive wormhole.

All tracks written by Diannov Pamungkas
Mixing by Nahash / Raphael Valensi
Mastering by Enyang Ha / Urbiks
Artwork by Spaceheadtr
Design by Jesse Pimenta
Remixes by Bagvs & Laenz

Vinyl distribution by Rubadub

The first installment in the Dance Data Lathe series comes from Munich-based, veteran producer Zero Crossing — with a remix from none other than trailblazing producer Shiken Hanzo.

Andreas Angerer, aka Zero Crossing, began creating his own music in the mid 90s. This release marks the return of the project via Dance Data and his first full EP since 2006.

'Brain Wash' dives into familiar yet sonically fresh territory, bringing the Zero Crossing sound full circle into 2024. Some listeners might initially draw comparisons to artists like Christoph De Babalon, Photek and even Shiken Hanzo himself — but they'll also notice a unique thread that is entirely Angerer's own.

Each song conveys a sense of isolation and being lost in an unfamiliar space — elements that, intentionally or not, bind the EP together. They traverse through a thick and ominous jungle, searching for a light in the darkness.

Then, Shiken Hanzo's interpretation of the track 'death fog' infuses it with a hyperdriven edge. He effortlessly blends elements from the original with rhythms and tones one wouldn't think possible — all the while building up steam for a head-swirling climax.

Mastered by Zero Crossing
Remix by Shiken Hanzo

The first installment in the Dance Data Lathe series comes from Munich-based, veteran producer Zero Crossing — with a remix from none other than trailblazing producer Shiken Hanzo.

Andreas Angerer, aka Zero Crossing, began creating his own music in the mid 90s. This release marks the return of the project via Dance Data and his first full EP since 2006.

'Brain Wash' dives into familiar yet sonically fresh territory, bringing the Zero Crossing sound full circle into 2024. Some listeners might initially draw comparisons to artists like Christoph De Babalon, Photek and even Shiken Hanzo himself — but they'll also notice a unique thread that is entirely Angerer's own.

Each song conveys a sense of isolation and being lost in an unfamiliar space — elements that, intentionally or not, bind the EP together. They traverse through a thick and ominous jungle, searching for a light in the darkness.

Then, Shiken Hanzo's interpretation of the track 'death fog' infuses it with a hyperdriven edge. He effortlessly blends elements from the original with rhythms and tones one wouldn't think possible — all the while building up steam for a head-swirling climax.

Mastered by Zero Crossing
Remix by Shiken Hanzo

ALBUM OUT APRIL 08 2025. 

We’re thrilled to welcome back Konalgad to Dance Data, this time with his debut LP, “Club Dream”. Spread across two discs for maximum fidelity, this is sound system music with grooves primed for mixing and dialed-to-a-Tee bass weight, but hovering above the grounded structures are fleeting rhythmic textures that veer things off into a world worth getting lost in. Throughout its 11 tracks, “Club Dream” plays out like a full mix, ebbing and flowing through a variety of energy levels and moods. Some of the range you’ll find here includes half-time dream-step, peak time pulses, and dubbed out mid-tempo tech, all done with a cohesive restraint and appreciation of atmosphere. The record imparts it’s own kind of dance floor dream logic onto the listener, inviting us to let go of making sense of things and trust in its fuzzy logic.

We are incredibly excited and grateful to present 'NOCTURNO' - the first proper LP release by Chilean producer, Masot. The 10 tracks effortlessly traverse multiple genres throughout the album arc, showcasing a highly detailed and carefully designed sound palette - one which remains remarkably intact throughout the whole journey.

Moments of Nocturno feel melancholy and pensive, but never void of the hypnotic and percussive 2-step rhythms that feel like a darker take on the historically upbeat sound of UK 2-step and Garage.

Each song is meticulous, but not over-indulgent. The intricacy, melodic elements and club utility allow the LP to be as functional for the club as it is for at home listening.

released May 25, 2024

All tracks written by Tomas Fernandez Quijada aka Masot
Mastering by CZ Wang
Artwork by Jesse Pimenta

This is a compilation of artists making electronic music outside of the cities which are historically renowned for dance music. Coming from Oklahoma City, we believe contemporary media should be accessible by anyone, regardless of where you live. All of these artists are indirectly connected through their drive to make something of where they live, not to try to make their hometown exactly like Berlin or New York. Instead, these artists take what is unique about their home-cities and amplify those idiosyncrasies to make something both rare and adventurous.


This is for them as well as anyone else living in a small town who wants to make dance music, throw raves, put out records, etc. We hope you reach out to people on this cassette. The night-time belongs to us, and we don’t have to dream alone.

Skulptor's first release of 2025 on CatalogWorks follows last year's successful single "FeltThat" with the same beguiling Latin Glitch Pop soundscaping they are known for. The difference is found in the distinct separation of both tracks, all written in Mexico City. "Loisada Mama" is a post-future dancefloor hit armed with uplifting chaos that's violently euphoric, driven by a projectile bullet beat. "W3theartz" (wet hearts), a homage to male tears, pivots into a sensual glitch-hop ballad armed with an unheard-of hook-bop that's both addictive and sweet. The EP features remixes from Bronx NYC's most prolific producer El Blanco Niño and Montreal-based slow-tech heavyweight SIM.

"Music is meant to be shared" - this is the defining ethos of pi pi pi, a multidimensional platform manifested for the music lovers, listeners, and dancers of our known universe. Whether it’s taking shape as a digital haven of music sharing, a conductive frequency of electrifying amusement, or a side quest with a friend in a lucid dream, pi pi pi has existed as an amorphous zone of (un)reality to inject some spritely silliness and funny fun back into the seriously serious seriousness too often found encroaching the joys of danceable electronic music.

True to its inquisitive nature and quest for fluidity, pi continues to evolve into new & enticing forms - this time, expanding it’s amoeba into a label and connective energy accumulator to bring forth Oscar Huang's debut EP "Slipstream". This first EP release for both pi & Oscar is a collection of tender dispatches recorded amidst the tumultuous landscape of the pandemic, but centered on motion and transcendence in spite of that.

Longstanding collaborators & Bay Area based experimental duo Kush Arora & Lucas Patzek aka Only Now & Orogen return with ‘AVULS’, the project’s sophomore release.
 
Building on the unearthly, black hole transmissions and creaking, exospheric ambience of their self-titled debut, Only Now & Orogen present an abyssal, elemental broadcast from another unchartered extra-terrestrial zone. Remote and astronomical yet tied to a newfound sense of rhythmic structure, ‘AVULS’ navigates a course through inverted beat-led frameworks, surging detonations of sub-bass, and severely turbulent, monumentally scaled soundscapes.
 
Amidst this large, slow-moving cyclone of sound sit fragmentary emergences of choral voices and Gregorian chants; a distant, esoteric presence within dense eruptions of attritional noise and infinite recesses of low end.
 
In harsh, pointillistic detail and through infernal surround sound, Only Now & Orogen channel dub, noise and power electronics, evoking a distorted, ritualistic inflection on the Voyager Golden Record; a mass of tectonic motion and friction; a storm in deep space.
Only Now is Kush Arora, Orogen is Lucas Patzek.
Mixed at Ancient Owl Audio, Berkeley, USA.
Mastered by Sam John at Precise Mastering, UK.
Artwork by Andrzej Masianis, Poland.
Recorded in Oakland, San Francisco, and Sonoma, California in 2019

‘Timeslave (II)’ sees Kush Arora’s Only Now project return with renewed intensity, in the sequel to the formative Infinite Machine release ‘Timeslave (I)’.

After the groundbreaking hybridity of the debut volume in the ‘Indian Unclassical’ series, the emphatic riddim-focused explorations of dancehall, bashment, and drill found on the Club Yeke EP ‘Vision’ – released under Arora’s own name – and select live dates alongside the likes of Andy Stott, Debit & Nyege Nyege-affiliated metal pioneers Duma, ‘Timeslave (II)’ finds Arora invigorated by aesthetic variation and constructive collaboration.

Enlisting renowned, specialist percussionists including Iggor Cavalera (co-founding member of Sepultura), Dave Sharma (Sub Swara) & Ravish Momin aka Sunken Cages, Arora adds symbiotic fuel to the fire, infusing the resonant, largescale sound world of the Only Now project with raw, frenetic insurgencies of virtuosic instrumentation.

Set within devastating productions that venture into graphic drone, hyperkinetic drum sequences, dub ruination (‘I Am Remembering’), writhing, cataclysmic noise (‘Shiv – Vengeance 2’, ‘EVP Inversion’), and even, degraded, introspective doom metal interludes (‘Endless Defeat’), the restless rhythms of Arora’s collaborators add unprecedented dimensions to the resolutely dynamic material of the Only Now project.

As in most cases, the words don’t do justice to the sound, the map really isn’t the terrain and you’re better off taking the time to explore it all for yourself.

In the heart of Los Angeles' endless traffic buzz, a sonic collective emerged, championing the idea that higher BPM music need not be harsh or monotonous. Recently, their mantra, "Fast Not Hard," faced scrutiny: could it truly endure, or was it simply an idealistic phase?

Just as doubt peaked, an unexpected helicopter delivered a mysterious capsule, possibly from the future—or aliens. Inside was tangible proof of their philosophy: a sleek disc containing three original tracks that captured their ethos. Embraced as sacred scripture, it was named "Soft Fascination," embodying their nuanced approach. Group member Carré became their inaugural leader, charged with spreading this musical gospel.

Carré preached through "Soft Fascination," merging classic dubstep basslines with gentle melodies, gradually evolving toward accessible, rhythmic structures. "Glowing" highlighted simplicity and clear, spacious sounds, while "Cute Mad" radiated playful positivity and lively bass.

Before returning home to refine this ethos further, Carré recruited two distant disciples: Priori, who transformed "Soft Fascination" into an industrial soundscape, and James Bangura, who expanded "Glowing" into a profound, melancholic experience.

Thus, the "Fast At Work" movement solidified, its principles proven spiritually, musically, and physically. With Carré soon passing leadership onward, the future alone—or perhaps those enigmatic aliens—knows the true reach of their gospel.

“Chop chop chop”—as the rhythmic reckoning approaches, we rave disciples remember the roots of our journey and its vibrant evolution. Past scripture recalls our beloved helicopter's arrival, delivering a sacred capsule from the future—or perhaps aliens—containing tangible proof of our enduring "FAST NOT HARD" belief. Yet, we understand all philosophies must evolve.

Thus, we celebrate the birth of the HOVER CAPSULE, a sub-disc expanding our sonic gospel through handpicked apostles, each illuminating distinct visions of musical ascendance. Side A presents foundational heli-dogma: first matriarch Carré teams with legendary phonic guru Addison Groove, joined by rising duo Baalti and London underground's Adam Curtain, crafting hymns of rhythmic unity. Side B dives deeper into emotional expressions of tempo. Ruby May Moon & Emanuel offer poetic intensity, while Introspekt elevates the message through dissonant two-step spirituality. Finally, Data Plan & 11:68PM encapsulate an ethos forever expanding—hovering gracefully forward.

“Isla Diferente” is the title of the new album by Apulian producer Andrea Mangia aka Populous. It’s the first release on his newly founded label, Latinambient, a name initially conceived to describe the sound of the album, which later evolved into a sonic manifesto and record label. 
All the tracks were written between January and February 2024 during an artistic residency in Lanzarote. “Isla Diferente” (Different Island) is the nickname of the most mysterious of the Canary Islands. A unique place, shaped by lunar landscapes, silent volcanoes, untouched nature, and art. Andrea spent a month at Hektor, a finca in Los Valles, in the heart of the island, surrounded only by hills, crops, and farm animals.
Lanzarote served as the backdrop for the creation of an album that seeks to explore its peculiarity through contrasts. Blending the ethereal sweetness of ambient music with the physicality of electronic and experimental latin rhythms, “Isla Diferente” attempts to capture the essence of an austere and wild place, where the lightness of the wind clashes with the hardness of imposing rocks, and where the white and green of the houses starkly contrast with the darkness of the volcanic soil. The album’s soundscapes evoke the vibrations of ecstatic dance, a movement that blends motion and transcendence through particular healing frequencies.

H.D. Reliquary is the first eponymous release from Ben Shirken [a.k.a. Ex Wiish], and finds him returning home to 29 Speedway. The songs sparked during sessions with close collaborators - across 11 pieces, artists such as Pavel Milyakov, MIZU, Dorothy Carlos, Kevin Eichenberger and Muein breathe personality into the record. H.D.R. coaxes beauty from a serrated, raw, yet subdued palette drawn from improvised recordings of trumpet, violin, upright bass, cello, Max/MSP and modular synthesis.

The title references the hard drive as a sacred container for relics, contemplating how digitally archived fragments of one's existence can burn eternally after death. Archives, and in this case recordings, splinter and warp. Some distort what they contain. Some vanish, and others are eternally preserved, immune to deletion. Your information on these digital drives becomes archival shrapnel, the music that survives the remnants of collaboration.

Quick to note the dangers of creating music with ecologically intensive, mass marketed, and unethically trained AI software, Shirken employed bespoke, resource-light machine listening techniques for some of the compositional process. Pieces of recordings were fed into a series of proprietary neural networks, generating MIDI information and audio that reacted to on-the-fly soloing, imaginary sessions between players and algorithms invented posthumously.

With Threadline & Rush, the third double single from The Songweaver, Merlin Modulaw delves into the project’s more synthetic and otherworldly side. These tracks are defined by icy, swirling synths, metallic drums, and fast-paced, trance-like melodies. The result is both haunting and euphoric—a soundscape that feels suspended between tension and release. The synthetic textures and driving rhythms create an almost hypnotic energy, while the melodies weave through the tracks like echoes from another realm. There’s a ghostly, untouchable quality to the sound, yet it retains an undeniable emotional pull. This release captures Modulaw’s ability to craft immersive electronic worlds that are at once coldly futuristic and deeply human, offering a glimpse into the darker, more frenetic side of The Songweaver.

Spectral Bounce’s fifth instalment comes courtesy of L.A.’s rave archivist and dancefloor operative Dreams, A.K.A. Jesse Pimenta. Throughout his decade-long career the California native has inspected, dissected and concocted all manner of dance musics, leaving his mark with drops on Apron Records, Pinkman, BANK NYC and his own imprint Dance Data. On SPEC05 — Dangerous When Wet — he hijacks the synapses with 4 accomplished productions, plotting a high BPM course through manifold styles using the raw aesthetic that characterises his output.
